reason: E1 and E2 support the link between grain refinement and enhanced passivation in a Ti-based alloy, but neither addresses Q235 steel, chloride environments, or the role of impurity segregation. E3 discusses grain boundary energy and segregation in a different alloy system but does not provide direct evidence for micro-galvanic corrosion in Q235. The key premises thus lack specific prior evidence for the target material and conditions.
premises: Grain refinement increases grain boundary density and provides more nucleation sites for passivation
Grain refinement promotes formation of thicker, less defective passive films
Impurity segregation at grain boundaries can form micro-galvanic couples and accelerate localized corrosion
The proposed mechanism applies to Q235 low-carbon steel in chloride environments
